newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TIMELINES - Today in History - April 17.
newsitem.headline: TIMELINES - Today in History - April 17.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian Magistrate HENRY BAYLISS, who was once shot in a gunfight with bushrangers MORGAN and CLARK (and later had the bullet removed and mounted on his watchchain), was born in 1826.
Australian pioneer pastoralist ALBERT LE SOUEF, who became a director of the Melbourne Zoo, was born in 1828.

Russian politician and Prime Minister (1958-1964) NIKITA KHRUSHCHEV, was born in 1894. Following problems with the Russian economy, and conflict with the United States over the Cuban Missile Crisis in 1962, he was ousted by LEONID BRESHNEV and ALEXEI KOSYGIN. KHRUSHCHEV died on the 11th of September, 1971.
American dramatist and novelist THORNTON WILDER, whose book "The Matchmaker" was adapted to become the musical "Hello Dolly", was born in 1897.
Pioneer Australian anthropologist and explorer ALFRED HOWITT, who rescued the sole survivor of the BOURKE and WILLS expedition and spent many years living among Aborigines, was born in 1830.
Australian racehorse owner and trainer ERIC CONNOLLY, whose success in punting brought the popular saying "the luck of ERIC CONNOLLY", was born in 1880.
Dutch bandleader and composer JAMES LAST, was born in 1929.
** EVENTS **
1194 : The second coronation of King RICHARD I of England
took place upon his return from the Third crusade.
1421 : More than 100,000 people died at Dort in Holland,
when the sea broke through the dikes.
1492 : CHRISTOPHER COLUMBUS received a commission from
the Spanish monarchy to explore the western ocean. 1521 : MARTIN LUTHER was excommunicated by the Diet of Worms.
1725 : Englishman JOHN RUDGE left 20 shillings a year in
his will, for a poor man to be employed to wander through the congregation of the Trysull Church in Staffordshire, ensuring parishioners were awake!
1790 : American diplomat, scientist and author BENJAMIN
FRANKLIN, died. He once said "In this world, nothing is certain but death and taxes".
1860 : The first boxing bout took place between an
American and an Englishman, in Hampshire, England.
1895 : The Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed, whereby
China and Japan recognised the independence of Korea, and Formosa was ceded to Japan by China.
1919 : Leading film-makers CHARLIE CHAPLIN, MARY
PICKFORD, DOUGLAS FAIRBANKS and D. W. GRIFFITH joined forces to launch their own company, called United Artists. The Corporation began by producing a number of epic adventure films.
1924 : BENITO MUSSOLINI's Fascist Party won the Italian
elections.
1944 : All of Sydney's daily newspapers, plus the
Melbourne "Herald" and the Adelaide "News" were seized for defying censorship regulations. They were published with stories censored.
1953 : Comic actor CHARLIE CHAPLIN announced from his
home in Switzerland that he would never return to the United States, following repeated accusations that he was a communist.
1956 : The Victorian Health Commision declared the

asbestos industry was dangerous. The government moved to control the use of asbestos following a finding that workers who'd contacted the substance recorded a high level of asbestosis. The controls included the use of breathing apparatus and exhausts and restricted use for those over 18.
1960 : American rock star EDDIE COCHRAN died in a car
crash in England.
1961 : A small force of about 1,300 Cuban exiles failed
in its bid to topple the communist regime of FIDEL CASTRO. The force ran into the Cuban Army, soon after landing at the Bay Of Pigs, and its members were either killed or captured.
1964 : The Rolling Stones released their first L.P, "THE
ROLLING STONES".
1970 : The crippled American spacecraft Apollo 13

splashed down safely in the Pacific. The three astronauts, on board, were safe and well. They'd spent 90 hours travelling through space after an explosion in the service module, which housed the main engine and oxygen supplies. The planned moon landing was abandoned as the crew raced against time to make a re-entry. The three had to travel in the cramped lunar module for most of the homeward flight.
1980 : Rhodesia became the independent State of Zimbabwe.
1982 : The Polish Solidarity organisation became legal
after a 10-year ban.
1984 : 25 year-old British Police Constable YVONNE

FLETCHER was killed, when a peaceful demonstration in London's Saint James's Square turned into a battlefield, as a gunman inside the nearby Libyan Embassy began firing into the crowd. 10 other people were wounded.
1986 : El Al security staff at Heathrow Airport found a
bomb in the luggage of a pregnant Irish girl, placed there by her Jordanian boyfriend.
1986 : An anti-smoking campaign was launched in China,
featuring a 2 year-old baby who reportedly smoked 4 cigarettes a day and cried if he was refused a light!
1990 : Moscow imposed a blockade on Lithuania, in a bid
to stem demands for independence.
1996 : Police gunned down 19 landless peasants in one of
Brazil's bloodiest massacres.
